main_answer_reason: The report accurately reconstructs the two batches, most core dates, the opposed trial/District Judge/High Court dispositions, and the two requested munafa grounds. It nevertheless relocates the District Judge’s 1910-possession premise from its actual first-batch quotation, blurs the first-batch trial cutoff with the distinct second-batch delivery cutoff, attributes unsupplied legal reasoning and an unrecorded patnidar argument, and states without support that munafa grounds become relevant only after a reversal of the post-possession set-off refusal. It also omits the important second-batch Privy Council additional-rent holding and specific accounting/period details. These issues prevent treating the substantive analysis as wholly supported, without establishing the withheld Supreme Court outcome.
uncertainties: Only the supplied CASE/LAW excerpts are available: the deciding Supreme Court reasoning and disposition are withheld; none is inferred here.
The report quotes the District Judge’s since-1910 premise while first-batch actual delivery was August 1913; the source establishes the inconsistent attribution but not why the judge stated 1910.
For first-batch trial deductions, the source says date of assessment of mesne profits; the relationship between that phrase and the date of delivery of possession is not resolved by the excerpt.
The allowed sources give the High Court’s decision to reject later set-off, but not its reasoning, so procedural-timeline and distinct-causes explanations cannot be verified.

The additional Order XIX, rule 4 grounds were sought at the hearing; the excerpt does not specify their admission, final procedural treatment, or whether they reach pre-possession munafa calculations.
The supplied LAW extracts include various statutes, but they do not establish that those enactments governed the historical claims; no statute is used to fill missing case facts or reasoning.
